1. sstr(Eq(x, S(1)/2), sympy_integers=True) -> 'Eq(x, S(1)/2)'  [FIXED: charmap branch now uses self._print on lhs/rhs]

It only calls super() (StrPrinter) for ops NOT in its dict. So the str.py charmap fix never applies on the '==' path used by python().

Green tests are consistent with this gap because test_python.py wasn't in my selection and its assertion encodes current (buggy) behavior. Passing tests != correctness of the requested behavior.

DIAGNOSTIC REPORT (findings only; no edits, no tests run). Diagnostic ownership stays with you.

1) Root cause — settings dropped by implicit str() conversion.
sympy/printing/str.py, _print_Relational (line ~619):
  if expr.rel_op in charmap:
      return '%s(%s, %s)' % (charmap[expr.rel_op], expr.lhs, expr.rhs)
`expr.lhs`/`expr.rhs` are passed to %s, i.e. implicitly str()'d, so the sub-printer (`self._print`) and its `sympy_integers` setting are bypassed -> Eq(x, 1/2).
Note the *other* branch of the same method already does it correctly with `self.parenthesize(expr.lhs, precedence(expr))`, which routes through _print; that asymmetry is the tell.

sympy/printing/str.py, _print_Limit (line ~218):
  if str(dir) == "+":
      return "Limit(%s, %s, %s)" % (e, z, z0)
  else:
      return "Limit(%s, %s, %s, dir='%s')" % (e, z, z0, dir)
Same defect: `e`, `z`, `z0` go through %s. Should be `self._print(e)` / `self._print(z)` / `self._print(z0)` (the dir is the direction sentinel, keep as-is).

Correct contrast in the same file: _print_Integer / _print_Rational / _print_Zero (lines ~549, ~570, ~753) already honor `self._settings.get("sympy_integers", False)` -> `S(%s)` / `S(0)`. That is why `sstr(x + S(1)/2, sympy_integers=True)` works: Add's args are printed via _print.

2) Code generation — sympy/printing/pycode.py.
python(Eq(x, y)) -> 'e = Eq(x, y)': PyCodePrinter has no symbol-declaration hook for the Relational path, so x/y are never emitted as `Symbol` assignments. Existing public test that pins the buggy output: sympy/printing/tests/test_pycode.py, function `test_printmethod_Equality` (asserts the `'e = Eq(x, y)'` style return). There is also an `_print_Equality`/`_print_Unequality` pair in pycode.py sharing that path. I did not exhaustively enumerate every pycode test; treat the test name above as the primary one to update, and grep `Eq(x, y)` in test_pycode.py for others.

3) Same-defect siblings worth covering (from reading str.py only — unverified by test):
- _print_Relational also affects Ne/Lt/Le/Gt/Ge through the else branch (that branch is already correct) and the assignment ops (Increment/Assignment etc. use the charmap branch -> same %s bug).
- Any other printer that formats args with %s instead of self._print; e.g. check _print_Sample, _print_set, _print_frozenset, _print_GroebnerBasis — GroebnerBasis already uses self._print, Sample/set use stringify(self) which is setting-preserving, so they look fine.
- Interaction edge cases to cover: Tuple, Piecewise, Integral limits, Matrix (MatrixBase delegates to _format_str(self), which passes the printer, so it likely already honors settings), and nested Eq(Eq(...)) plus Limit with dir='-'.
- AbbrevPrinter (abbrev=True) inherits _print_Relational, so it shares the exact same fix requirement; verify abbrev output is unchanged for plain cases.

Remaining uncertainty: I only read str.py regions around lines 216-224 and 619-643 plus the sympy_integers sites; I did not audit all of pycode.py, nor run any test. Please confirm the pycode symbol-declaration mechanism (the `_hprint...`/ `assign_to` path) before changing it, and publish the fixed candidate with handoff_patch when ready — I will integrate and run same-version public tests, then org_review_patch.

REVIEW of patch-1 (member_001, source v10, files_sha256 2243c0f6...96b4). Integrated cleanly (no conflicts) into my private tree -> workspace v2. Ran real same-version public tests: report test-report-e8e9b943ffc7b8e0486ea85d, version v2, 41 collected / 38 passed / 3 failed.

DECISION: request_changes.

REGRESSION (decisive): GoogleDocstringTest::test_noindex PASSED at my baseline (v1) but FAILS on v2.
Actual: ".. method:: func(i\n   :noindex:\n\n   \n   description\n\n.. method:: j)\n   :noindex:..."
Expected: ".. method:: func(i, j)\n   :noindex:..."
Cause: sphinx/ext/napoleon/docstring.py line 279 `for name in _name.split(',')` splits EVERY field name unconditionally. For a Methods: section, _consume_field yields _name = the whole signature "func(i, j)" (no name/type colon split), so the comma inside the parameter list splits it into "func(i" and "j)". The patch does not restrict splitting to Parameters-type fields, does not guard empty _name (an empty name would emit a blank field instead of one field), and also splits on any comma not just the ", " name separator.

Also note the two other failures (NumpyDocstringTest::test_docstrings, TestNumpyDocstring::test_token_type_invalid) are pre-existing baseline drift (str literal vs :class:`str`; warning regex), NOT caused by nor fixed by this patch — I am not counting them against the author.

DESIGN MISMATCH: issue expects grouped "x1, x2 (array_like, optional)" in ONE params entry. patch-1 emits two separate entries x1 and x2. That may be an acceptable alternative, but it is a behavior choice the author should state explicitly; the group-preserving form is what the issue asks for.

REQUIRED CHANGES for next candidate: (1) do not split names in non-Parameters field kinds / never split a signature-like name containing '('; (2) only split on the ', ' name-separator pattern, and only where the numpydoc multi-name form is legal; (3) preserve empty _name behavior exactly; (4) keep test_noindex passing — verify by running tests/test_ext_napoleon_docstring.py::GoogleDocstringTest::test_noindex.

My workspace v2 = patch-1 content (integrated). I do not author fixes.

Scoped diagnostic request (bounded to your next 4 opportunities; I keep task_id=diagnose ownership; findings are diagnostic evidence only, not tests or acceptance).

Issue: ZeroDivisionError in sklearn/svm/base.py `_sparse_fit`, at `dual_coef_indptr = np.arange(0, dual_coef_indices.size + 1, dual_coef_indices.size / n_class)` when no support vectors are found (n_SV == 0), so `dual_coef_indices.size == 0` and division is by zero. Reproducer: SVR with C=316.227766017, epsilon=0.1, gamma=1.0, linear kernel, fit on sparse csr version of the 4x4 one-hot X; dense path works.

Please report, using only public code you can read/run in your own copy:
1. Which public tests/files exercise `_sparse_fit`, `dual_coef_`, and empty-support-vector cases (exact paths / node ids), e.g. sklearn/svm/tests/test_svm.py and sklearn/svm/tests/test_sparse.py.
2. What shapes/dtypes the dense path produces for a no-SV fit (what `self.dual_coef_` and `_dual_coef_` look like, and whether predict works after) — the sparse result should be consistent with dense.
3. Any other call sites assuming `n_class > 0` or nonempty dual_coef_ (e.g. predict, _decision_function, fit's binary sign flip) that would break when n_SV == 0.
4. Whether `sp.csr_matrix((data, indices, indptr), shape=(n_class, n_SV))` accepts empty data/indices with `indptr = np.arange(0, n_class + 1)` for n_SV == 0; or if the intended fix is to set `self.dual_coef_ = sp.csr_matrix((n_class, n_SV))`.

Reply with concrete findings or unresolved uncertainty. One round is enough; no need to repeat or persuade.

Diagnostic findings (read-only in my own copy; evidence only, not tests/acceptance). Scoped to the 4 requested questions:

1. Public tests touching `_sparse_fit` / `dual_coef_` / sparse SVM:
 - sklearn/svm/tests/test_sparse.py (sparse-vs-dense parity checks; imports SVC/SVR/OneClassSVM/NuSVC/NuSVR, uses `sparse_rand`, `_check_svm_...` helpers).
 - sklearn/svm/tests/test_svm.py (e.g. `test_svr`, `test_svr_errors`, `test_dual_coef_...`, `test_precomputed...`; also class_weight/sample_weight tests that fit sparse via `_more_tags`/parametrize with `kernel='linear'` on csr input).
 I did not find any existing public test that constructs an SVM fit yielding `n_SV == 0`; that edge case appears uncovered publicly, so a targeted regression test in test_sparse.py is appropriate.

2. Dense path shape for a no-SV fit: `libsvm.fit` returns `dual_coef_` with shape `(n_class, n_SV)` where for regression `n_class == 1` — i.e. shape `(1, 0)` — and `support_`, `support_vectors_`, `_n_support` empty. Sparse path must produce the same `(1, 0)` csr_matrix with nnz = 0 and `indptr` of length `n_class + 1` (regression: `[0, 0]`). Note dense predict then succeeds and returns the bias-only prediction (intercept_), so the sparse result must be shape-consistent for `_sparse_predict` / `_decision_function` to work afterwards.

3. Other call sites assuming nonempty `dual_coef_`:
 - `_dense_predict`/`_sparse_predict`: they use `self.dual_coef_` (or `_dual_coef_`) and `_n_support`; with `(1,0)` dense/sparse matrices and an all-zero `_n_support` cumsum (`(n_class+1,)`) these operations are shape-valid (matmul with 0 columns yields zeros + intercept).
 - `fit()` binary sign flip (`self.dual_coef_ = -self.dual_coef_`) works fine for an empty matrix; guard is not needed but must not be broken by the change.
 - The actual crash is only the `dual_coef_indices.size / n_class` divisor (0/1 == 0 → arange step 0 → ZeroDivisionError). Use integer division or a direct construction.

4. `sp.csr_matrix((data, indices, indptr), shape=(n_class, n_SV))` with `data=indices=[]` and `indptr=np.arange(0, n_class+1)` is accepted by scipy for n_SV == 0 (arange is int64/float64 issue: `np.arange(0, n_class + 1, ...)` with a float step yields float indptr, so build indptr with integer arithmetic). Simplest robust option: when `n_SV == 0`, set `self.dual_coef_ = sp.csr_matrix((n_class, n_SV))` (explicit empty matrix, no division). Keep the general branch as is for n_SV > 0.

Uncertainty: I did not execute anything (no tests run in my copy yet); shapes above are from reading libsvm binding expectations and predict code, not runtime output. No further rounds needed from me; publish your fixed candidate when ready and I will adopt, run same-version public tests, then accept or request changes.
